newsitem.title: USA: Hershey Foods net income surges on strong sales.
newsitem.headline: Hershey Foods net income surges on strong sales.

text.p: Hershey Foods Corp. said Friday its earnings rose nearly 25 percent in the second quarter, driven by strong sales growth in its North American chocolate business.

Second-quarter net income hit a record $50.6 million, or 33 cents a share, up from $40.8 million, or 26 cents a share in the same year-ago period. Revenues rose to a record $906 million from $796 million a year ago.
The results edged out analysts' forecasts of 32 cents a share, according to a survey by First Call, and Hershey's stock rose $1.125 to $55.19 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.

The company cited robust sales in its Hersey Chocolate North America division, fuelled by revenues from Leaf North America, a confectionery business it purchased from Finnish group Huhtamaki Oy late last year.
Promotions tied to the film "Lost World" also boosted income, it said.
However, the sale in late 1996 of the company's European operations, as well as a slight decline in revenue in its pasta and grocery group, somewhat offset the revenue growth, the company said.

Hershey said the second half of 1997 will be "a challenge," with both the integration of Leaf and the absence of profit contributions from the divested European businesses expected to diminish earnings.
Hershey Chairman Kenneth Wolfe also said it will be difficult to measure up against the strong second-half posted in 1996.
"In the aggregate, however, 1997 will be another excellent year for Hershey Foods," Wolfe said. He sees the company reporting record sales and profits again at year-end.
